utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. If I may, I merely wish to inform you about something and make a request. The translation service tells us, as we have indicated, the witnesses that are about to come should be priority. I have just been informed that the expert findings will be done by the 1st of May, so could -- so could the Chamber please bear this in account. We were told we would have to have them ready by the 24th of April but unfortunately the translations will simply not be ready by that time so please could the deadline be extended to the 1st of May?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think last time we made an oral ruling that you should submit the expert statement in two weeks, which is at the end of April. It's more or less the 1st of May. So upon your request, I believe that your request is granted. The submission of the expert statement will be extended to the 1st of May. You may sit down, please. It seems to me that we have great problem with the translations and in order to have the translation to catch up, we'll have a longer recess, which is about a week, after finishing the present witness, we'll have a recess until Wednesday next week. Mr. Usher, will you please bring in the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, may I remind you what I told you yesterday. Please focus, look at the screen and slow down, please, because it is indeed very difficult for our interpreters to work when we speak over each other or when we are too fast. So please bear this in mind. Witness, yesterday we broke off when we were talking about the Heliodrom and you were describing to us how many units were quartered there and you explained the name "camp." Today, I'd merely like to ask you whether there was also a military prison at the Heliodrom called the central military prison. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. There was the central military prison at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, I'm looking for a photograph which I want to show you with the usher's help. Mr. Usher, can you please help me? It is the Exhibit 20.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, in this courtroom, we have heard from different witnesses that these buildings were used for prisoners. Tell us, are you aware of that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And could you please make a circle around it and point at it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates] This building with the flat roof, and there were -- the command of my brigade was in this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in the building next to it? In this larger building?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: According to the transcript, counsel asked for photo -- Exhibit 20.7. But that does not appear to be the photo that's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which number? I could not see. 17? This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Usher can you help us. What number of exhibit is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 17. THE USHER: 20.17.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Because the transcript shows 20.7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 17, okay, and 20.11.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I will now show you another photograph and perhaps on this other photograph, you will be able to identify.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph is much clearer. This building with the flat roof that I'm pointing at now is the command of my brigade. Across it is the boiler house used to heat the Heliodrom. What I'm pointing at now is the canteen and to the right are the kitchen where the food was prepared and restaurants.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the building to the left, do you know who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building to the left, when Juka Prazina's troops came they would be accommodated in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now I'll give you my copy, because we cannot draw anything on this one. So would the usher please give you this copy? And will you put number 1 where your command was, number 2 where the boiler room is, number 3 by the canteen, and number 4 by Juka Prazina's units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was this? Excuse me I've forgotten. Number 1 is the command two is the boiler house, three is the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the building below the canteen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the facility where food is prepared and restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you then put number 4 there and number 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This that I'm pointing at now was the surgery, the infirmary of the garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And will you put number 5. Did you ever see any prisoners in this building number 5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, let's move on and let me ask you, was your brigade of a mixed ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, we did not really go into that all that often but during a certain period of time, when we conducted an analysis, a survey, of the strength of my brigade, then I can give you literally the data down to one to ten men but on the day of the 8th of May, 1993, my brigade numbered about 2.280 or 2.270 men. Of them, there will be -- well, as I've said, this number will not be 100 per cent accurate, 1.080 members of the HVO who were Muslims, about 1.170 were Croats and 11 were other or, in percentage terms, as of that day, my brigade included 45 per cent of soldiers -- of Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you give us the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the 8th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Did its composition change? Were the Muslims with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That composition began to change, and I'm referring to those days and certain phenomena within my brigade -- in my brigade, which were the -- which were the result of the situation arisen between the HVO and the army of B and H in central Bosnia, and in particular, in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we received information that as early as January, there was an attack of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Konjic against the forces of the HVO which were not as strong, as numerous, and in March or more accurately starting from the 8th of -- that was the information that we received from Konjic, when Dr. Safet Cibo, that was what we were told, became the mayor of the municipalities Konjic and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you but the transcript does not say the 8th. You said the 8th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 8th of March, 1993. And then the relations suffered an additional blow, that is the large-scale armed attack started already against the units in the Konjic area, the persecution of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you once again, I'm sorry. Who attacked whom and what civilians were persecuted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croat civilians were persecuted and expelled and the attack, as I have already said, was launched by the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received this information personally too from an officer from Zvonko Zovko who came to Mostar from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the last name because it is not in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvonko Zovko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please spell out his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Z-O-V -- Z-V-O-N-K-O, Z-O-V-K-O.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now it's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He notified me -- he informed me in the operational zone of Mostar and we, that is we already -- that is since January -- we had this information, and I ordered my service for information and propaganda to draw up conclusions or better put, an information, and send it to all my units with a view to identifying all harbouring ill intentions out to destroy the joint struggle of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the HVO, or rather the Muslims and Croats in the HVO, and personally I was invited to Radio Mostar and in a programme, I pointed out to what could happen and what regrettably did happen subsequently if we did not identify those disseminating lies and sowing discord.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you describe some of the changes that took place in the relations between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can. I can tell you about the relations which I pointed out at the respect and joint struggle in four or five examples and I can also tell you about relations which produced some adverse effects.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say -- I did not tell this Honourable Court that at the

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: at the expense of professionalism but I took great pains to have proper representation, ethnic representation. I mean soldiers in my brigade and my command. So that I designated as my operations officer an acquaintance of mine from the Territorial Defence and who had called me after he'd been released from the Serb camp in Dubrovnik, that is, he was exchanged in Dubrovnik, the Serb camp was not in Dubrovnik, it was in Bileca. A Muslim, Salko Coric, I designated him the head of the -- as the head of the transportation service, I appointed a Muslim from Blagaj, from the 8th battalion, Ibrica Jazvin. As the head of the artillery, which is of course the most important firing power of any unit, I appointed Muslim Hajro Jakirevic and as the head of the military intelligence, I appointed Muslim Seno Salcin. At the time of religious holidays, the Muslim -- the Islamic Bajram, Catholic Christmas and Easter, the soldiers, that is Muslims and Croats in the HVO, took each other's place in manning the front line and they did so of their own will so that both could celebrate, mark, those religious holidays. The relations couldn't be more correct, and I can say that they were so good that even the officers in the command of my brigade, those were Muslims, paid visits to the homes, to the families of Croat officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you still owe me the answer. When did these relations change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first change in the relations, I began to sense in my brigade, when, in April, my operations officer, Muslim Salko Coric, told me that he was -- that members of the BH Army mistreated him, used to mistreat him when he crossed the old bridge on his way to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Salko Coric was of what nationality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim, Salko Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you be very precise whenever you're answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he told me that it became ever-more difficult for him to go to work. At that time, he brought me a painting, a work of art, made by his brother, a member of the BiH army, who was a painter, who graduated from art academy. His name is Avdo Coric, who was born in Nevesinje, as a token of appreciation for what I did for him. On this painting there is a berry tree. In fact, a bud, a genuine, true bud, which was not painted, which was put on to the painting and it was blossoming and there were these seeds of the flower scattered all over the painting. Later on, whenever I looked at this painting, I thought that this was perhaps the one and only way for my friend Salko to give me a signal that this unity is breaking up, bursting its seams. Another moment in time was the imprisonment of two members of the Siroki Brijeg battalion of volunteers. They were taking food to the Guberaca battle line which was located above the city of Gnojnice. In the course of their return, Marinko Covic and Karlo Zelenika were imprisoned, captured, by a group belonging to the BiH army, to be more specific, the 4th Corps of the army. This happened on the 5th of June, 1993. The troops confiscated their vehicle, a bus transporter, and they used this vehicle to collect Croats, members of the military police, at the Kovacin feature, checkpoint, along the M-7 route at a town called Bisce Polje and took them all together to a prison in Eastern Mostar, I'm not quite sure whether this was the SDK building or the 4th elementary school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you give us the date of the year when this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. It was the 5th of May. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1993. I apologise. Earlier, I said it was the 5th of June but it was in fact on the 5th of May, 1993. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I immediately informed my commander about this event. The commander of the operation zone southeastern Herzegovina, Mr. Miljenko Lasic. I was disgusted indeed. It may very well be that I used some stronger language at that time. The commander told me that I should calm down the whole situation, that these were rigged incidents, however isolated incidents, and that no -- that is every conflict must be avoided. At that time, I had a small problem with regard to the defence of the line because the colleagues of the prisoners withdrew from the -- from the defence line to the Ortijes airport, and I, in agreement with members of the unit in Gnojnice, I took this defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This line was with whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The defence line was with the JNA and the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you have any similar incident of this sort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Left from the Siroki Brijeg unit, there were also the 4th Battalion members stationed, who, however, had not withdrawn from the defence line. Upon the insistence of the operations zone, on the 7th, my soldiers were released from the prison. I asked them whether they had been mistreated, they told me that they were not, in terms of physical mistreatment. However, as soon as their vehicle had been confiscated on the rear view mirror which was located on the windshield, their crown was removed from that rear view mirror and it was thrown out of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you referring, to a rosary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to a rosary which is usually put on to the rear view mirror by the Catholics. When I thought that the whole situation simmered down and that this was everything that we might witness, on the 8th of May, 1993, [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: So Mr. Zeljko Kurtalic was sent to the collection area, and since we did not have a sufficient number of vehicles, he took the vehicle belonging to Dragan Milicevic, deputy logistics officer. This was a Zastava 101 passenger car. Members of the BiH army, and it was in a settlement called Mahala, in fact in this town of Mostar, intercepted him, took his vehicle, and they took him to East Mostar, to a prison there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When was he released from prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall the exact date. I think it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Roughly, month, year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: After about one month, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was the month, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was released in June. I do not know the exact date but it must have been towards the end. Was it the 26th or the 28th, I do not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did anything specific happen in April of 1993, as far as these relations are concerned? To be more specific, in Mostar or in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special happened in the area of my responsibility but in the town of Mostar, things did happen. In Mostar, as far as I can recall, it was somewhere in mid-April that an armed conflict took place. I cannot say who was the initiator, near the HIT building. It was a conflict between the members of the BiH army and the policemen on the Croatian side, i.e., on the HVO side, and some persons were wounded in this conflict. In order to calm the whole situation down, we held a meeting, which I also attended, between the commanders of the 41st, I think, Brigade of the BiH army, Midhat Hujdur, Hujka, and deputy commander of the operational zone, southeastern Herzegovina, Mr. Petar Zelenika. At that time, the commander of the BiH army, Arif Pasalic, and of the southeastern Herzegovina operational zone, Mr. Miljenko Lasic, were not in the town. They were left with the duty to sign an agreement concerning the definition of a demarcation line, which was jointly agreed upon as the line of movement and checkpoints were established along the route. On the left-hand and the right-hand sides, in the direction of the bridges, it was agreed upon to set up police checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you finish?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, I have a feeling that you are perhaps slightly too slow. I know that it's very difficult for you but still this is better than too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now request the Registrar to bring us Exhibits ID D1/106, 109, 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let us first take Exhibit ID D1/106. I will give you some time to read it. I'm interested in the last section, the Mostar report. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, I'm interested in this, particularly point 4. Do you know this document? Is this something that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this. The command of the 41st Brigade of the BiH army was located in the Vranica building, and it was very thoroughly secured, guarded, through an external secure and guard system. As far as I know, there was a double security system, i.e., the perimeter was very large. How this exchange of fire came about, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now have a look at the Exhibit ID D1/109. Could you first, please, check the date on page 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the report of the 19th of April, 1993, for the 18th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please once again focus only on the Mostar report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that on page 5 of the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English translation, that is page 6, report from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, obviously, these are reports sent in by the brigades from their battlefields and it is obvious here that the Serb aggressors attacked the 2nd Brigade, occasionally the 3rd Brigade. Two of my men died because they stepped onto land mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 5.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you tell us who were the two men who stepped on the mines in the minefield. Here they are mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djeko Enes and Jasaric who were members of the 8th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You were their commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: They are described under item 2 of this report. What else happened, or what else could you deduce from this report? Mention is made of clashes between HVO, VP and BH Army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the conflict was due to the exchange of fire from both sides and this is why a meeting was held on the 21st of April. The meeting that I had been describing earlier, when this sector was put under the control of the patrols of both sides' police, the HVO police, the BH Army police and the civilian police, as well as the international observers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will now show you document ID D1/110.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And would the Registrar prepare ID D1/108 and 124, please? And D1/125?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This was a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry. Will you please describe the document ID D1/110?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the information propaganda service of the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, issues a press release on a meeting held at the main staff and which was attended by General Philip Morillon, chief of the army staff Sefer Halilovic, chief of the HVO main staff Milivoj Petkovic, the commander of the 4th Corps of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Arif Pasalic, commander of the southeast Herzegovina operative zone, that is representing HVO, Mr. Miljenko Lasic; and representatives of UNPROFOR and the European Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you mean that is the meeting that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the meeting that took place at the main headquarters. And the meeting that I was referring to was at a lower -- was lower-ranking, that is, it was a meeting to discuss the implementation of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, usher, could you give him documents D1/108, D1/124, 125, D1/126? Madam Registrar, if you would be so kind, D1/126, 128 and D1/127. And we'll go through them document by document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: First, the document ID D1/108. Do you have it in your hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Will you describe the document to us, the date, who is the author and so on and the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will do that. The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the army of the Republic of BH, the 4th Corps command, reference number --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, you don't need to do that, just the date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostar, 17th of April, 1993. Addressed as a military secret, strictly confidential and as an urgent document, sent to all the units of the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who signed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was signed by commander Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what does this order say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have the documents. We have the translations already. If you have some specific questions, you could ask this witness but don't let him read it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In respect of this document -- I've been watching these. It appears that the previous ones come from the Zagreb archive. However, this document, 108, the source or the origin of this document is not clear to me and I wonder if we could get some information about the origin of D1/108.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The source of this document could be either the archive, I do not really know exactly because I have lots of documents, or the witness has brought it to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember if you gave me this document personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then it is presumably from the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have the exact list of documents that we took from the Zagreb archives and this document, I presume, features on the list. So there are over a thousand documents, we shall go through it and we shall provide the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now is probably not the time but as the Trial Chamber knows during the Prosecution case in chief, we were required to produce witnesses who testified as to the origin of the various categories of documents that were being submitted. Now this witness doesn't seem to know where this document came from. That doesn't mean that he can't talk about it. That's not my argument. But Mr. President, we think that certainly as the -- as a greater number of documents are submitted on the part of the defence, it will be our position that none of them can be admitted into evidence until there has been testimony as to the source of all of them, as was the case during the Prosecution case in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, so later on, would you please do your best to lay the foundations of those documents first? Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, Your Honours, but when I ask for the authentication of Prosecution witnesses or any witnesses, and documents which the Prosecution uses for cross-examination which I knew, and which the Court and the Defence see them for the first time, they say they are new because they introduced all these documents, they were admitted or not, but now we see that in their cross-examination, every day we are given new documents which we had never seen before. So I should also like to ask that they not be admitted until the gentlemen from the Prosecutor's Office provide us with a response as to their origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with this document? Or the incident? Do you know what happened? Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have read this order as you were talking and as a soldier, this order, to me, would seem quite clear, if that can be my comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But what do you personally know? Did it happen, what this order describes? What happened to it? Do you know anything? Do you know about what happened, the incidents on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you about the actions on the ground, from Konjic and then in central Bosnia and so on and so forth and I believe that this order had to do with some preparations for combat operations, aggressive, offensive operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it is now time for the break. And I believe this will be the best time to do it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, we have to speed up things just a little bit. But please always remember the interpreters, but we nevertheless have to move on a little faster. My first question concerning this document, this is D1/108, do you know, were you aware of this order issued by Arif Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about two orders issued by Mr. Arif Pasalic, and I suppose this one was there. Well, I can't exactly remember. But I knew one of his orders and I also told my soldiers about it. It reached me, I don't know how, but -- through what channels, but he said that Muslim soldiers should remain in the HVO and move over to the army only when he says so. So that was one order that I was aware of. And another order, when a meeting was held in the brigade that I commanded, and I said that the state of alert should be raised to a higher level, and there was -- and that order had the title and it said, "For the defence." But the elements of that order from the military point of view indicated that the intention, that the intention pursued was an offensive by the forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that order was signed by the commander of the 41st Mostar Brigade, Midhat Hujdur.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very good. Now the last question concerning this document, item 1 speaks and I see that in all the other documents, same thing, we have the HVO and HV forces. Did you ever see the Croatian troops, that is troops from the Republic of Croatia with your own eyes, in Mostar or wherever you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Troops from the Republic of Croatia sometime, I can't remember the month, but it was in the very early days, I saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm asking about 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, I did not see the troops of the Croatian Army, but in my unit, there were soldiers who had been before in the army of the Republic of Croatia and the same held true of the operative zone, that is the commander of a battalion was Zdenko Puljic, who had fought in the Croatian Army but he, as a volunteer, returned to his birth place and we had an operations officer, a Muslim of Albanian origin, Fadil Haljiti -- Sok. In the military district. I know about Jazvin Jaganjac, who came from the Croatian Army, a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Mostar defence. I also know the commander of the Northern Camp during the Mostar defence, a Muslim, Ibro Halilagic and scores of others, brothers Rupcic and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So during the aggression against Croatia, they were in the Croatian Army and after that, they went back to their birth places, is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And they were citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Counsel just put a leading question to the witness and it had been my intention to object to that before the witness responded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry for the objection being so late. Well, Mr. Krsnik, this is a direct examination so you are not allowed to ask any leading questions. If you want to continue, you have to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours. I just do not know what the interpretation was like. Of course I know that I may not ask any leading questions and you notice that I only ask one or two. They just escaped me during these four weeks so I do not know what the interpretation was. I only drew a conclusion from what the witness had said. I did not even ask a question. I was merely drawing conclusions from what the witness had stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in the transcript, you said very clear, "They went back to their birth places?" Is that so? You gave the answer first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, correct, Your Honours, because that is what the witness had said before that. He himself said that. Look at the question before it, where he himself said it. It was the witness who said they went back to defend their birth places, and I merely confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness said one person, one person, came back to his birth place, but your question is "they went back."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Your Honour. Yes, you're quite right, Your Honour. I apologise. You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, and what was the status of those people that you mentioned, I mean from the point of view of the army formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, like everybody else, they were considered volunteers who had returned to defend their native places, and I can confirm [indiscernible] were and his brother were born in Ljubuski and they belonged to the Ljubuski Brigade and furthermore they also commanded that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And they were the citizens of what country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1991 and in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I did not ask whether in 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was dual because I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to the next document. I'd like you to look at the document number D1/125, and D1/124. Please look at both those documents. And now that you've read it, look at the document 126. That is 124, 125 and 126.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, also 127 and 128.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, Witness, will you please read them all and then I will ask you a few short questions. Tell me, please, these documents speak for themselves but are you familiar with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Document D1/124 is not something that I knew about, and those other documents, that is 125, 125, 125, yes, I was aware of that document. 127 and 128, I was aware of them too, because I had read them in front of the unit that I commanded, as early as April, or better said, towards the end of April and the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. And did it indeed happen? Were these orders referred to? Did it come to pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is difficult for me to say that all that simply but a similar or rather an identical situation took place on the 9th of May in the morning hours, although it says here that it should have been at 18, 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, these documents relate to the 19th and 20th of April, and I think that the witness has not answered the question that was just put. Rather, he's moved on to the 9th of May so we ask the witness be directed to answer the question that was put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But maybe something in these documents is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. related to the incidents that happened on the 9th of May. We have to let this witness go for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I did not think that I was being asked whether this had happened on the 20th or the 19th. If that is what you're asking me, I can say that it did not, but that such an operation was carried out on the 9th of May, yes to this, my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Along these directions, and under these established codes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with some slight deviations. Whether they were codes for the signals units but these orders for offensive action was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, we are referring now to document D1/124. Do you know, Mr. Bajro Pizovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him very well indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He commanded a unit, a brigade, that is what they called it, Bregava. And he persisted in requesting the commander of the operative zone of southeast Herzegovina, Mr. Miljenko Lasic, to let him hold the line, the front line, in a place called Rotimlja, feature 690, summit Gradina. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you tell us, what is the unit that was under the command by -- of Mr. Bajro Pizovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this was the Bregava Brigade, a part of the ABH units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you finish --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] However, Mr. Lasic, the commander of the operative zone, insisted on this request made by Mr. Pizovic. A few days after the occupation of this defence line, Mr. Pizovic lost the line again because the Serb army moved it. [redacted] [redacted]. On one occasion, I visited him at his command in Rotimlja.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I understand. But, you know, this was going on for seven years. Thank you, Your Honour. At that time, I visited the command of the brigade and I saw some officers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Which brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bregava in Rotimlja, and I visited and saw some officers that I had known there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Being a professional soldier, can you tell us what is being ordered in this order, very briefly, in one sentence, because the document is self-explanatory, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this order, made by commander Bajro Pizovic or in both orders? Which are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The order issued by Bajro Pizovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see from this order, from this order one can see that the enemy that he mentions here are members of the HVO. Then, that they would have to be repulsed from Rotimlja and that communication should be cut off, that is the route M-7 should be blocked in the village of Buna, which means that they would have the southern Neretva valley under their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, in this Court, we heard a number of witnesses, members of the Bregava Brigade, who testified here that they had been captured by the HVO, detained by the HVO, in fact their testimonies referred to the period following the 30th of June, 1993, somewhere until the 15th or 16th of July, if I can recall it well, and that they had been detained only and exclusively for being Muslims. Since in your testimony today, you mentioned your defence line, which was Rotimlja, in fact these witnesses had been referring to Rotimlja and claimed that they had been detained there for the mere fact that they were Muslims. Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in July, I was not defending the Rotimlja defence line. That section was defended by the 1st Brigade, by the 1st HVO Brigade, because of the situation that persisted in another section of Mostar, and this situation developed in the period following June 30, 1993. I know, however, that in this section, as well as in the area under my responsibility, the town of Buna, the airport, Ortisje, and then towards the right, Kicini, these are all mountaintops and then right, towards the right, towards Rotimlja, on the 13th of July, 1993, an organised attack was waged along these sections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. Who waged the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. Did the Bregava Brigade participate in it to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any knowledge of that but I believe that they did, because they were located on my right-hand side. They couldn't have been in an isolated place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, my objection is that the witness, as he said, does not have any knowledge of that so I think beyond that point we are just engaged in speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, what we want to hear is what you did and what you see, your personal experience.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say that I have no knowledge about it, and I would like to have my words understood and interpreted literally, because I came here to tell the truth. I had knowledge of what was going on in the neighbouring brigade, but not as far as every detail is concerned. Nonetheless, what was going on for a certain period of time in my brigade as well, because we were neighbours, to Foda's Point. I know for sure the name of every soldier under my command who died, because I visit their families every year to commemorate the day of their death.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. Are you now speaking about the event that took place at the beginning of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: To make it shorter, what happened, who attacked you, how many people died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was attacked by the BH Army, which, in a vast majority of cases, consisted of troopers, Muslims, who used to be members of my brigade, and on that occasion, they killed Slavko Kulas, who left the house in pajamas and said...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour can we go to private session, because the witness cannot refrain from identifying individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: These police checkpoints unfortunately, none of them were -- are given in the transcript. Could you be kind enough to repeat them slowly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police checkpoints were agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. Before that, were these mixed points, checkpoints, or what were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, it was then agreed that both police forces hold their own checkpoints but that mixed police patrols be established along the Bulevar street towards the Arrow Hotel and Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to repeat where the police checkpoints were located and please do it slowly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police checkpoints were located, as agreed, towards the Bristor Hotel, towards the Titov Bridge, the public health centre, next to the HIT building, and I can't recall the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could we have Exhibit P11.8? No, P11.18? And I'll ask the witness to use the pointer to indicate the checkpoint held by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So that the Chamber can get the picture, you can even take a pencil, Witness, and you can circle those areas where they were located. Where was the BH command? Just use numbers, from 1 until wherever you go. Where was the HVO command? Where was the BH Army command, and so on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you better use different colours of the marker so that to distinguish the different sides.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If you are trying to find the HVO, black colour is for HVO is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then put number 1 on its command.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And also for the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Well, this is what I can identify now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you then for the transcript tell us which colour do you use to indicate whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used the red marker to mark the facilities, checkpoints, of the BH Army. And blue, and the blue marker to mark the command checkpoints of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You also mentioned the Carinski bridge but you didn't indicate any checkpoint there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I'm not quite sure where the checkpoint was so I'd rather not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So only what you're 100 per cent sure. So that is very good.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please not speak over the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where were you on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, I was in Mostar. I was in Mostar on the 8th of May too, because on the 8th of May, I had to go to visit my units, and around 2.00 or 3.00, I can't remember exactly, on the 8th of May, 1993, I was informed that Zeljko Krtalic had been captured and I went straight away to the operative zone of southeast Herzegovina to seek their assistance to ask them to intercede with international factors, to have the man set free. And I stayed in -- I spent the night at my colleague, Maric's place, in West Mostar, in a locality called Smrcinjaci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And your command of your brigade was still in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And your positions, where were you on the 9th of May, the area of responsibility of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of responsibility of my brigade was where it was in April, except that parts of the Siroki Brijeg volunteer battalion were at the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you had no units in Mostar? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no units in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, you mentioned 2.00 or 3.00 on the 8th of May, was it in the morning or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see, in the afternoon, very well. So you can proceed. You said you went to spend the night at your colleague Maric's place on the 8th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you the exact time but sometime in the morning of the 9th, it could have been 4.30 or maybe quarter to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, perhaps it will be easier for you. We have prepared a big map of Mostar so can I ask the usher perhaps as you tell us your story, perhaps we could use this map and point at these places to Their Honours and thus explain what went on that 9th of May -- 8th and 9th of May, according to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the number of this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D1/132. I asked the usher yesterday and today to make some room for this map. No, this map cannot be put here. It is just too big.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Usher I asked also yesterday that we must have a place for this map because it's very big. Sorry, I forgot. [Interpretation] Perhaps we could put it over the booths and put scotch tape to put it over the booth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, the interpreters must be able to see the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's quite early. Could I suggest we take our last break right now and then come back in half an hour and then go for the rest of the day and that would enable them to set up the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe, Mr. Krsnik, if you want to use a big map, you have to inform the Registrar and let them prepare for that. Well, okay. We'll break until ten past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, are you going to finish this witness this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are sorry but the counsel's microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, he said, "Yes." Mr. Stringer, can you see the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Not really, Your Honour. It's my understanding that the technical booth will be able to focus in and put it on the television screens so we'll see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very good. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Honours, I did give the Prosecution a copy of the map, a copy of the same map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Before we move on to the 9th of May and this map, would you be able to tell the Court, could you state better what you are telling us? We are still talking about one of your soldiers who was arrested on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if I'm correct, it was Zeljko Krtalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But do you know if some other HVO soldiers were detained one of those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. On the 8th, that is on the 7th, [redacted] [redacted] Toma Lasic was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Slower. And please, Witness, be so kind, I and the Chamber cannot really anticipate what you will say. [redacted],

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toma Lasic was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who else, how many men, number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was detained near the Neretva Hotel. When I asked those who had been detained, they said that on the -- in the evening of the 8th, there were 20 Croats detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were they exchanged later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, there was an exchange. Whether they were all exchanged, I do not know. I know about some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now another question. Between the 9th or 10th or the 11th or the 12th of May, until the 30th of June, were there any incidents until the 30th of June, in Mostar, of course, if you have any personal knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no conflicts and perhaps if there were any incidents they were not worth mentioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean until the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the technical booth now let us see the tape so as to finish with this group of prisoners? The translations were handed over both for the Chamber and for the interpreter's booth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The Croatian side procrastinated with the prisoners. About some 400 civilians that were exchanged on both sides. Everthing was done with a five-hour delay because of the exchange lists. The commander of the Muslim units in Mostar, Arif Pasalic offered many civilians, Muslims to which he had personally issued [indiscernible] right Neretva bank. It is interesting to note that no Croatian soldier was taken prisoner in direct Muslim-Croat conflicts but when returning from the defence lines towards the Serb aggressor. I was transporting [indiscernible] captured on Monday morning at 6.20. I was taking the water, you know, up there to the main road and then two soldiers came running out of the wood in front of me, then they took me out of the car the other took the [indiscernible] to the car. I was in detention for 18 days. I was arrested in the apartment and how did it that happen. Well, my next-door neighbours, they came to the door with a rifle. This unfortunate man was physically mistreated at the Drace prison. The first day were the hardest when my nose bled because of the blows and I probably had a minor brain concussion but they gave me no x-rays, no pictures. I was dizzy all the time and I kept falling down. In the former SDA building, turned into prison, there was no physical mistreatment. We were not physically mistreated. There were individual cases but we were not mistreated by and large. Nobody hit me but the food was bad, there -- you couldn't take a bath, you couldn't wash your face. I did not change my clothes for 90 days. You could wash your hands only and garbage was collected every day. It was dirty. You can not imagine a routine medical examination at the Mostar hospital the following medical finding was given. There is a total of 37 patients of whom four are civilians 33 soldiers, of them two were wounded, one gravely, and the one sustained light injuries. The former case has a fracture of the upper leg, mostly a wound from explosion, while the others mostly we have several of them who had suffered injuries by blunt instruments, altogether the situation rather good, satisfactory."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is D1/50, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, first, did you see this on Croatian television? Do you know those men and do you know when this exchange took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see it on television. I cannot remember exactly when the exchange was but I think it was sometime around the 26th or maybe the 28th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26th or the 28th June. I cannot remember exactly. I cannot remember the date exactly. But -- and I recognised here soldier Toma Lasic and I recognised also another soldier who was a member of the Siroki Brijeg volunteer battalion, Miljenko Puljic called Piga. He was detained in the area of Bugre Plahovine at a place called Dracevice as he was going to his positions on the 9th of May, together with Igor Covic, Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And as for this TV tape, we said that they were in the prison called the SDK. Is that the SDK you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the self same and there was only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where was this SDK building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDK building was near the building of Dracevica building near Tito Street, on the east side, controlled by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now I'd like you, Witness, to stand up. You have a microphone here but take your pointer with you. You will have to take your earphones just in case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just a point of caution, Mr. President, and I don't know whether they are able to keep the witness's face protected at the time he's standing at the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Could we go to the private session. Just for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We ended with this meeting of a sort.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard about this meeting and after the meeting, an order was made to cease with all the armed operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did ceasefire begin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How long did it go on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It went on until the 30th of June, 1993, as I had elaborated upon it before, when the BH Army attack was launched on the Northern Camp on the 30th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, can we discuss the 10th of May, 11th or 12th, as far as I'm concerned. Can we now speak about the establishment of the defence line inside Mostar town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could speak about the establishment of a defence line but at that time, we had peace and ceasefire there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us, after this ceasefire agreement, how were the HVO troops and units deployed in Mostar, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have some knowledge of that. They were deployed -- in fact they were divided among three sectors, the entire zone was divided into three sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The zone or the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The zone of the town. So all the way from Bakina Luka to the destroyed Carinski Most bridge, there was one sector. The second sector stretched from the Carinski Most bridge to the grammar school. And the third sector was the sector from the grammar school to Podhum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Before we discuss the structure of command in Mostar, would the usher please be kind to give you documents from D1/114 to 122? From D1/114, 115, 116, 117, 119, 120, 121, 122. Would you please browse through these orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just been reminded by my colleagues that in the transcript, document D1/118 is omitted but it was given to the witness by the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Question to you, as a professional soldier. If an army, armed forces, are preparing an attack, how long in advance should this be prepared? For example in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on the capabilities of the command preparing it to do so, but it must certainly be in a period of seven to 15 days in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What can you see in these orders, or do you know the orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with them and the orders show that weapons, the weapons that had been available to the op zone, operative zone Mostar, so one could see which were available for the op zone Mostar and which belonged to the units inside the town of Mostar, which did not provide the security sufficient to -- or the power sufficient to use them to prevent further escalation of the attack operations launched by the BH Army. Therefore, the commander of the operative zone used, in fact, exercised his right to provide for additional interesting weapons and troops and bring them from Citluk, 20 kilometres away, and from Ljubuski, 40 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are these orders indicating that the army troops were not ready and prepared at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the scale and the power of the attack is concerned, well, judging on the basis of these two factors, one can say that they were not prepared at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed. Can you tell us who is the commander in the sectors that you had mentioned in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sector 1 is...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could we go to closed session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Private or closed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Private or closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Private session, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then sector north, which covers Vojno and all the way to the area of Planac, towards Rakitno and then the sector called town, Grad, which covers the city itself, and its suburban neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who is in command in these new sectors then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sector 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't have to give us the names but tell us who is above them in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When was the operative zone command established in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere at the beginning of July, I don't know exactly the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Now I'll give you a specific question. Who is the commander of the units deployed along the Bulevar street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command -- the defence command of the town of Mostar is -- well, in terms of management, organisation and defence matters, is in the hands of the operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: To be more specific, let me ask you the following: Who is the commander of the units of the 4th Battalion, ATG Benko Penavic, ATG Vinko Skrobo, the 9th battalion and the military police battalion as they are deployed from whom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm not clear exactly what the period of time is now that we are talking about, because there appear to be changes that the witness is talking about in the structure or the command in the region of Mostar and so if we are going to talk about the units positioned along the Bulevar, we'd like to know what periods of time specifically and under whose command they were with in these specific periods of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. You may clarify that for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we are all listening to what is going on in this courtroom from the 12th of May until the 30th of June. The witness explained everything, and then he explained what happens at the beginning of July, when the city defence command took over, and this is the periods I was putting my questions about at this point in time. In June, they were divided into three zones. Now they are in sectors under the command of the city defence. I think that we only need to go step by step, and I'm sure that the translation, interpretation, is not that bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm trying to follow closely and understand. I just want to have a good understanding of what the witness is saying, that's all. In my view, counsel is not directing this examination in a way that leads to the most clear and fullest understanding of the structure of these units during the various periods of time that he's been talking about so I respectfully disagree with counsel about the clarity of his direct examination on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think the Prosecutor is entitled to have those matters clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, from the 12th of May to the 30th of June, how was the city of Mostar divided and who is in command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was divided into three sectors, and I already gave the names of those who were in command in the respective sectors. This was the operative command along the defence line. And each unit that had its own members deployed along the defence line at that time had to take care about tour of duty and about the need to get new members to be able to perform all the duties. However, it was generally believed that this type of command did not meet the requirements, and the operative zone had the right to reorganise along the lines in which, according to them, the defence would perform the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Who is in command at the beginning of July, in command of the units that are deployed on the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units that perform the defence assignments in the Bulevar, in the sector of the town, is under the command of the commander of the sector called town, Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can anyone else, in addition to him, give orders to the units along the Bulevar street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chain of command is known. The commander of the operational -- operative zone can give orders also to smaller, lower units, just as the chief of the main command can give orders to the units under his command directly, which was not a very fortunate solution in practical terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How the shifts organised along the defence line and where do the troops having performed their shift go, having finished their duty along the Bulevar defence line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shifts were determined depending on the conditions or circumstances under which assignments were carried out. When it was very hot or very cold, the shift lasted for three or five days, and when the weather was normal, it could take seven days. After completion of their shift, the troops went to their respective homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think there is a question that this witness has not answered yet. Before the objection raised by Mr. Stringer, you asked, "To be more specific, let me ask you the following: Who is the commander of the units of the 4th Battalion, ATG Benko Penavic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I was going to ask, Your Honours. I wanted to ask him this to clarify things first generally but as of now, I can assure you, Mr. President, I'll be very specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, let us make clear whether these soldiers have their garrison -- their barracks, their garrisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So where do they go having performed their shift along the defence line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: They go to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Which are located where? For example, where are the homes of the troops, members of the 4th battalion, Benko Penavic and Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know it, most of them were in the location of Banovac, then in Panjevina, Podhum, in other words, in the zone which they in most cases also covered along the defence lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Once again, the same question, who is in command of the 4th Battalion? We are moving from Podhum towards the secondary school, the 4th battalion, ATG Benko Penavic and then I'll ask you to explain what is in fact ATG, ATG Vinko Skrobo and the 9th battalion. You know we are moving from Podhum towards the secondary school. Who are the commanders of these units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: For sometime, the 4th Battalion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On the defence line along the Bulevar Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They would change because the commander of the 4th Battalion had been wounded. Therefore the 4th Battalion was under the command of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We are not interested. We are not interested in the commanders of these units. I want to know who were they under the command of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the town defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could anyone else, in addition to this person, also issue orders to these units until they are deployed on the Bulevar, the defence line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you before how the chain of command went, in the HVO, orders could be issued at different levels and some command levels could be skipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If I understand you well, from more levels than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more levels than one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, let me give you a specific -- put a specific question to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you. Could Mladen Naletilic give orders to the units deployed in Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could Mr. Mladen Naletilic issue orders to the units deployed along the Bulevar, Vinko Skrobo or any other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he could not, because he was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Had he not been a civilian, could anyone issue orders to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I told you who could issue orders to these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In logistic terms, who is -- who provides the supplies to these units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logistically, in the op zone and in the military organisation, these units are supported by the logistics of the zone in which they are performing their assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Tell me, another ATG which did not have a permanent defence line, like the other two mentioned before, when they would reach the defence line, could they operate independently, any ATG, for example the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: For example, you, as the commander -- for example, need the assistance of an ATG and you bring them in, they come to your position. Who is the commander of such an ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I ask for their assistance and the cause of this is the fact that we cannot carry out the assignments with the troops that are available, and assistance is usually sought by addressing myself to the operative zone of eastern Herzegovina, the troops that are sent to help me, until they had finished their assignments, would be under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, one question my colleague reminds me that I forgot to ask you. And where is the logistics physically accommodated in Mostar or somewhere else, I don't know really, but my question is where is the logistics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The logistics in Mostar, it was in two or three different places depending on the means. Part of the logistics was accommodated in the compound of the brigade command. That was my case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Uh-huh. And what about those units which are on the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That logistics was in Mostar and whenever -- whenever people are sent to the defence line, a sufficient combat gear is provided and at the request from the logistics base.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, did you have your unit on the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the period under consideration, I had a part of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into private session, because the identity might be disclosed again just for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you ever see at those meetings in the army command, did you ever see Mr. Martinovic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did either of them have a rank in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not know if they did. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When were the ranks introduced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
