utterances.text: I think sometime when the reorganisation started. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. I cannot really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And until that March, 1994, how was the commanding -- the chain of command organised? How did you issue your orders or any other commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through respect, one commanded and the example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. By respecting authority and behaviour. And were the commanders elected from the lowest ranking unit to the highest one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, I'm looking at the questions. Witness, did you ever see Mr. Mladen Naletilic at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when somebody -- I'll say it, the Convicts Battalion, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean how we perceived the Convicts Battalion or how was it established?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, I always try to remember that the indictment has to do with 1993. So when we say the Convicts Battalion, what is it? Where is it? You know what I mean. I mean what does it cover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion is a formation unto itself and we saw that it was formed by men who were persecuted, punished, under the communist system and it brought together the best guys from Siroki Brijeg, and unfortunately, houses were few and far between from which some father of the family did not serve his communist term. For instance, my father --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let us slow down. It is true that we are coming to the end but let us slow it down. You said that your father was singing and therefore he -- you have to explain to the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can quote you the song, if you would like me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, there is no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let's skip this question. Let's skip this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where was the Convicts Battalion quartered or rather where did those men live, if you know? And did the Convicts Battalion ever, to your knowledge, man a section of the segment of the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where did they live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of them lived in Siroki Brijeg, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was there barracks in the Siroki Brijeg where members of the Convicts Battalion lived, do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: There has never been barracks in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what was the tobacco station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said it yourself. Those were buildings -- those were buildings that belonged to the tobacco factory but they had been destroyed. And one couldn't sleep in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And was there a prison at the tobacco station that you would be aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, we are moving towards the end of our examination. I will show you a couple of documents. Do you know something about the Juka Prazina's unit? Do you know who Mr. Juka Prazina is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do not know exactly when he arrived. They told us that he arrived across Igman from Sarajevo and his unit was put up in the compound in which the brigade command was. I saw him often on a bike, riding around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will show you P234 -- P249, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, it's no problem. 249.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is this unit commanded by Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here, "Mr. Juka Prazina to be designated the commander of the unit."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who founded this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see the signature of the head of the defence department, so it is the defence department in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you whether you know it because it says it is affirmed here that Mladen Naletilic had it under his command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My colleagues warn me that I forgot to ask you another question concerning the Convicts Battalion. Will you now be so kind as to explain to Their Honours how does the Convicts Battalion go into action? Who calls them up? Who commands them? What is nature of that unit? Slowly. I think it is my last question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion is, from my military point of view, a special purpose unit for more complex combat missions, requiring better armament, more -- higher valour, more determination more military prowess, mental and physical fitness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who calls it, how he calls it and when it gets there, where it was called, who commands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically I say when I needed it and I needed it on the 19th of September, 1993, so I called them and I asked through the operative zone, not it, I asked for assistance from the operative zone, and who it turned to then, I do not know, this unit -- a part of the unit or a larger part of the unit or that unit arrived to the place I needed and performed the task I required.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when it came to you, who -- under whose command was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ordered what needed to be done in the combat sense of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said 19th of September if I heard you well, which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how long was this unit with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly how long, but I say four, maybe five days. They went in two directions because I was commanding at the time the sector north, my sector had been attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And could it be that it was with you on the 23rd, 23rd of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Barazic led the unit that was with me and it was with me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, do you know, in 1993, who was the Convicts Battalion commander, to your knowledge? Let us move to the private session because I have another question that has to do with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think before we get to the second question, my suggestion would be that we not move into private session until we've gotten an answer to the question that was just put to the witness, which was, who was the commander of the Convicts Battalion? I don't think that requires us to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm asking that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this case, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And my very last question: It was alleged here that the Convicts Battalion was in Rastani on the 23rd of September.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the Convicts Battalion followed the direction of Jedrinje for me and see who was there and who was killed there, and on that occasion, it was established who was killed there, and that someone -- followed the direction of Golubici and Marko Clanac to recover the lost positions and once again hand them over to the home guards to look after them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I merely wish to notify you that our questions and our time we have ceded to Mr. Krsnik so we do not have any questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I'm afraid it's time for the break. Witness, as I warned you yesterday, during your stay in The Hague, do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. I'm afraid we have to keep you for another day. We'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.
